verdicts.reason: Every quote verified verbatim. 11.08.01-licence-scope-grammar.md:46-55 is a nine-row axis table including `Data use` (:48) and `Grantee scope` (:55); :104 resolves a point carrying all nine; D-15 (:229) 'Grantee scope is an axis - licensee plus permitted assignees/sublicensees'; D-06 (:220) data use is separate. Against that, five files enumerate six: 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:63 and DT-07 (:199) and D-09 (:240) all assert 'the scope grammar has NO counterparty axis'; music-licensing-cx.md CX-16 (:146) and CX-18 (:29); 11.02.01:46; 11.03.01:26; 11.04.01:31. A grep of the whole domain for 'grantee' returns only 11.08.01 - no file reconciles the two readings. The contradiction is load-bearing, not cosmetic: 11.08.01 D-15's grantee values ARE party identities (licensee + permitted assignees), and 11.04.02 D-10 keys buyer blocks on 'the declared transacting party and the declared end client' - the same entities. 11.08.01 D-05 makes axes support exclusion, so a policy CAN key on grantee. That falsifies the stated rationale of 11.04.02 D-09's two-key-spaces model, of CX-18's 'the fold cannot fold buyer blocks / the aggregate is incomplete by construction', and of 11.04.01 Q-05's buyer-allow-list rejection. Two normative statements ('Grantee scope is an axis' vs 'the grammar has no counterparty axis') cannot both hold, and three [DEEP] files dated 2026-07-23 sit on the later, wrong side of an owning [DEEP] file dated 2026-07-16. Blocking retained. NOTE the finding is overstated on its AI-training branch: 11.08.01 D-06 (:220), its edge case (:122) and DT-04 (:172) are emphatic and 11.07 owns consent, so no competent implementer would encode training as a media value from 11.02.01:46's parenthetical alone. The grantee/counterparty branch alone carries the blocking severity.

All four quotes verified verbatim. 11.08.01:217 D-03 reads 'Instances pin the grammar version at *request creation* and carry it unchanged through pricing to issue | Refines the breadth pass's "pins at issue"'; DT-13 (:181) explicitly REJECTS pinning at issue as racing 11.03.01 D-02; 11.08.01:107 'the grammar pins at request'; :139 'the pin is taken at request creation'; and 11.08.01's Cross-Cut Notes (:192) instruct the sibling by name: 'it must carry `grammarVersion` pinned at **request**, not at issue (D-03 refinement, DT-13)'. 11.08.02-licence-certificate-issuance.md contradicts on three lines while citing D-03 as its authority: :55 'Grammar version | Pinned at issue (11.08.01 D-03)'; :145 'The instrument pins the version **in force at issue** (11.08.01 D-03). If the agreed scope is not expressible in that version, **abort**'; :186 'pins its version at issue'. 11.08-licence-instrument-lifecycle-cx.md:34 and :38 repeat 'pinned at issue'. 11.08.02 is [DEEP] and dated 2026-07-23, later than 11.08.01 (2026-07-16), so the stale reading is the newer text and carries the citation. Nothing in the tree reconciles them. 11.03.01:90 D-02 confirmed verbatim ('A price that moves between offer and acceptance is fraud, not a race condition'), so the divergence lands on an irrevocable instrument. Two normative statements about the same rule, each citing the same decision id, cannot both hold, and 11.08.02:145's abort path exists only under the losing reading. Blocking.

Quotes are accurate but the divergence is resolved in three places the finding did not weigh. (1) 11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-cx.md:82 (CX-05 synthesis Q5) raises this exact question and answers it: 'whether a work can be one-stop with attestation but no encumbrance declaration (i.e. is silence on sampling equivalent to "no samples"?). **Silence must not mean clean.** Provisional: both required.' (2) 11.02.01 does not assert the opposite - its own DT-14 (:159), which the finding cites only to dismiss, states the resolution directly: 'Their track may contain an undeclared Splice loop or an uncleared sample (11.02.03 - `encumbered` with a perfect ownership record) ... No shortcut: every work goes through all four inputs', and its edge case :130 lists 'may have an undeclared sample' as a reason a single-owner work is not one-stop. (3) The finding also conflates two objects that 11.02.01:79-82 separates explicitly: '`one-stop` is not a verdict. It is a separate derived boolean' - so 11.02.03 D-02's 'an undeclared work is not one-stop' is a statement about the badge, not a missing verdict enum value. 11.02.01's four-input list at :92 is a summary that does not contradict any of this; the residual (what encodes 'asked and answered nothing borrowed') is a mechanism question the sub-domain CX owns and has provisionally decided in the direction 11.02.03 D-02 and 11.05.01 D-05 both take. No competent implementer reading the unit's CX plus 11.02.01 DT-14 badges an undeclared work one-stop.

Quotes verified, but two premises fail. (1) 11.02.01:122's row is titled 'Attestation is contested mid-gate' and maps cleanly to the LISTED-party species only - 11.02.02 D-12 (:209) and its edge cases (:129, :130) draw exactly that distinction in the tree's own vocabulary: a co-owner 'contests' (invalidates the attestation, hence `incomplete` is correct), a non-listed stranger 'claims' (does not invalidate). 11.02.01:122 does not collapse both species; it addresses the one whose name it uses. (2) The finding's claim that there is 'no buyer-facing rendering' is false: 11.02.02:130 gives it verbatim - 'Buyer: "Contested - an authorship claim is open on this work."' - and the States table :158 carries a `Contested` row with the same copy. The behaviour is fully determined in the owning file: gate blocks new issuance, attestation is not auto-invalidated, issued licences stand (11.08 irrevocable), routes to domain 24, buyer sees the claim. What is left - which internal enum value carries it - is an encoding concern for a later layer, and the only genuine residual is tracked: 11.02.02 Q-04 (:218) 'Does a verified non-listed authorship claim drop one-stop, or only mark the work `contested`?', owner User, deferred to `/create-prd-security` after parent Q-01. Two implementers converge on the behaviour.

The central claim - 'no file says which component evaluates them or what result they produce' - is contradicted by the owning file. 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:89 states 'There is **no window in which a blocked scope can pass the gate** (D-15). Authoring is atomic; evaluation is at request time'; D-15 (:246) states it again with the enforcement point named - 'evaluation is at request time; **the gate re-checks fresh at issuance**. Catalogue lag is a display property, never a licensing one'; :63 fixes the timing ('At request time only'); :136 names the firing moment ('at next request, for a buyer block (D-09)'); :185 confirms the block is 'already in force' during withdrawal cleanup. The result maps onto 11.02.01's existing `blocked` verdict ('A standing policy or veto refuses this scope', :65) via 11.04.01:37's step-1 refusal check. CX-18 (music-licensing-cx.md:29) is not a silent gap - it is the tree deliberately documenting that the 11.04.03 fold excludes buyer blocks by construction, precisely so the reader does not look for them there. 11.02.01's five-input list not naming a buyer parameter is an incompleteness in a summary enumeration, not a normative statement that the gate never sees a buyer; its own happy path :86 admits requests that inherently carry one ('a quote request, or a licence attempt'). The residual is wiring, owned by /create-prd-architecture, not invented product behaviour.

Quotes verified, but the same table row that says 'queued' answers the divergence the finding says it forces. 11.01.05-dual-licence-coordination.md:64's 'What User Sees' column reads: 'Second buyer: "This work is on hold for another buyer until [date]. [Notify me if it releases]"' - a notify-me subscription, not a durable auto-granting waitlist position. That copy is character-for-character the same shape as the loser copy in the file that owns holds: 11.01.04:51 'Loser: "Just taken - [work] is on exclusive hold until [date]. Notify me if it lapses?"', in a row whose outcome column reads 'the second fails closed. Never both-granted.' So the loose word 'queued' in 11.01.05 (a [PARTIAL] file) is qualified in place by its own rendering and converges with 11.02.01 D-12 (:198), 11.02.01:115, 11.08.02:123 and 11.01-sync-licensing-cx.md:36, which all say refused-not-queued plus a notification. The second-call hold type at 11.01.04:33 is a hold a buyer affirmatively requests, not a state a losing racer is placed into, so it does not supply a competing reading either. No implementer builds an auto-granting queue from a row whose user-facing text is 'Notify me if it releases'.

The citations are accurate - 11.02.02 Q-04 (:218) is now a different question and 11.02.04:66 and 11.02.01:120 still point at that id - but the claimed consequence ('a decision the two files agree is open is owned by nobody') is refuted by the very line the finding quotes. 11.02.02 DT-07 (:171) does not defer the question, it deletes it with a stated answer: 'a category error, and rejecting it deletes an open question rather than deferring one ... Copyright is inheritable property; on death a writer's share passes to their estate. The party set is therefore unchanged ... Under D-04's shipped-ratio design this costs the work a displayed number, not its commercial life. The old Q-04 ... is withdrawn.' The residue it hands to 11.02.04 is the CONSENT problem, and 11.02.04 discharges it in its own edge case (:66): 'A party is unreachable / dead / erased | Permanently non-one-stop for scopes needing them'. 11.02.01:120 states the same outcome ('Permanently `consent-needed` unless an estate is enumerated in 09') and D-17 (:203) fixes the erasure mechanics. The finding itself concedes 'None at the behaviour level'. What actually survives verification is a stale citation to a reused question id - a reference nit, not an untracked product decision.

Quotes verified at 11.02.01:201 (D-15) and :155 (DT-10), and it is true no open question tracks a minimum-sample number. But the decision draws exactly one bright line and draws it decidably: D-15's hard prohibition is '**Never a point estimate for a party with no history**', and its three-way branch is `instant` / median-where-a-response-history-exists / '"unknown", stated plainly, otherwise'. 'Has a response history' and DT-10's 'responded enough times to have one' both resolve to n>=1 on a plain reading - a median exists at one data point. The edge case at :129 confirms the intended cut is zero-vs-nonzero, not a sample-quality floor: 'Cold start - no response history for any party | No time-to-clear is shown for `consent-needed` (D-15).' An implementer who imposes n>=10 is adding a rule the text does not leave open, not resolving one it left ambiguous. The 11.01.02 Q-03 comparison does not transfer: that parameter is a k-anonymity disclosure-control floor whose own text says 'What is left is the two parameters', i.e. the spec there declares the gap; D-15 declares the threshold.

Verified on both sides. 11.08.01 D-08 (:222) states 'A term may have **no computable expiry date** ... 11.08.04 must treat "no computable end" as first-class'; its edge case :128 '"Life of copyright, worldwide" | Has ~249 different expiry dates ... There is no single expiry date'; its Cross-Cut Notes :194 route three named cases to 11.08.04 - (a) no computable end, (b) term-uncommenced whose trigger the platform cannot observe, (c) option exercise. A full grep of 11.08.04-licence-amendment-expiry-lifecycle.md for 'computable', 'life of copyright' and 'territor' returns ZERO hits. Its expiry model is a single T-minus-N countdown (:35, :58, D-03 :103); its only non-standard row is 'Perpetual licence (creator, 11.06.04) | No expiry' (:64), which is not the same object as a term with ~249 jurisdiction-dependent ends. Its three Open Questions (:111-113) cover wrongly-issued licences, the supersede invariant and narrowing amendments - none the multi-date term - and the 11.08 sub-domain index's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 do not either. An explicit, named obligation from a [DEEP] owning file to a sibling is undischarged with nothing tracking it. Severity held at warning rather than raised: 11.08.01 D-08's 'first-class, not a null' forecloses the finding's wilder branches (earliest-date / latest-date fabrication), so what an implementer must invent is the state's rendering, the warning behaviour and the verification answer - not the whole semantics.
